gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 11 build entry now runs the gpio_wdt, bcm2835_wdt, and dw_wdt starter tests together with the dw_wdt survey gate so the simple-driver watchdog tranche stays reviewable in one place.

A dedicated survey gate now records that the dw_wdt starter, probe summary, registration handoff, and dedicated tests already exist while keeping the remaining platform-facing gap explicit instead of letting the current scaffold overclaim parity.

The survey note now anchors the live dw_wdt cleanup packet to lane `P11-L12` on `master` `0ddb982b08ffa3f1a34bddc0520f50af0b3e346f` so later runs can extend the same Phase 11 slice without rediscovering whether the registration handoff already landed.

The bounded starter already derives fixed TOP timeout windows, mirrors reset-mode versus IRQ-mode timeout selection and pretimeout bookkeeping, and now exposes a probe-time summary alongside register-image transitions without claiming platform-backed behavior.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep fixed-top limits, custom-top ordering, probe-time bookkeeping, registration-handoff selection, reset-mode and IRQ-mode timeout behavior, restart intent, and non-stoppable stop semantics reviewable around the landed starter.
The slice note now records the exact starter contract so the repo does not blur the current in-memory driver model into clock, reset, IRQ, debugfs, or hardware-backed parity.

The starter now includes a tiny probe-time summary around fixed-versus-custom TOP sourcing, nowayout and restart-priority bookkeeping, stop-on-reboot intent, and already-running watchdog state before any platform-backed behavior lands.

The starter now includes a small registration-facing handoff that keeps watchdog info selection, parent linkage, timeout-programming intent, and the bounded register-device handoff reviewable before any live clock, reset, IRQ, or MMIO work.

The next honest bounded step is a platform-backed registration and hardware-validation plan that can attach the landed handoff summary to real clock, reset, and IRQ ownership without widening the current simple-driver slice prematurely.

Platform-driver registration, clock and reset acquisition, IRQ registration, suspend and resume handling, debugfs support, devicetree TOP arrays, and live MMIO validation remain blocked until the lane grows platform-backed registration scaffolding around the newly landed handoff plus a hardware-validation plan.
